title: A machine-learning connectome separates SuperAgers from Alzheimer's disease and tracks cognitive vulnerability
summary: A sparse SVM on resting-state fMRI connectivity defined the Alzheimer's Resilience-Vulnerability Connectome, which distinguished SuperAgers from AD (AUC 0.85, N=290) and replicated in N=143. In cognitively unimpaired adults, AD-like individuals showed faster cognitive decline, greater amyloid-beta accumulation and higher conversion risk. The AUC comes from cross-validation; observational imaging, and two GWAS loci (CLYBL, FRMD6) are exploratory.
ai_technology: Sparse support vector machine on regional functional connectivity
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; Lehigh University

evidence.tested: 10-fold cross-validation in the discovery cohort (N=290), independent replication (N=143) and longitudinal outcome analyses.
evidence.unknown: Causal relevance of the connectome and the exploratory GWAS loci.
evidence.ai_role: The SVM classifier weights defined the connectome.
